title: Introduction to The Standard for Project Management
coreMove: Before choosing a method, read the Standard's frame: audience, purpose, and shared terms tell you when to use principles as judgment, not as a replacement process grid.

exampleSpecs.audience: PMO leaders moving a mixed organization to the Seventh Edition
exampleSpecs.stakes: prevent the formal standard from being misread as a shorter process manual
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the expected celebration of a 2021 consensus standard reveals a hidden wish for the old process grid

exampleSpecs.audience: project managers explaining the edition shift to delivery teams
exampleSpecs.stakes: stop a chat thread from turning the Seventh Edition into a renamed Sixth Edition grid
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the message exchange shows the lesson between short replies about 49 processes and the new reading path

exampleSpecs.audience: trainers introducing the Standard to sponsors and team members
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep a routine class from teaching process compliance before professional purpose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist interrupts her own routine and restarts from the Standard's audience and purpose

exampleSpecs.audience: consultants observing how shared vocabulary affects coordination
exampleSpecs.stakes: show how the old grid can sit in ordinary work without telling people what a word means
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a close observed moment shows the teaching point without a decision fork

exampleSpecs.audience: analysts tracing why a compliant project still missed the outcome
exampleSpecs.stakes: locate the interpretive miss that turned guidance into mechanical compliance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the failure is already visible, and the one decisive misstep was skipping the opening frame

exampleSpecs.audience: sponsors explaining the edition shift without oversimplifying it
exampleSpecs.stakes: recover from a sponsor's own slide that turns the Seventh Edition into a replacement matrix
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist notices his own error mid-briefing and corrects the frame before the room copies it
